output.narrative_summary: This result rests on the link from Automation Coverage to Response Time. If that coverage drops towards a lower level, more runs could support a different option. In this model, 64% of runs supported Automate Tier One Triage.

story_headlines.opt_automate: Automate Tier One Triage reduces response time by cutting tier one volume before it reaches engineers.
story_headlines.opt_hire: Hire Two Support Engineers would need higher ticket volume or weaker automation coverage to gain more support.

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in about 73% of variations, with medium confidence overall.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: The link from Automation Coverage to Response Time is the main point of fragility in this result.
stability_factors: Ticket Volume shows a steadier relationship to Response Time, with comparatively higher confidence.
fragility_factors: The link from Automation Coverage to Response Time could flip the comparison if coverage falls.

output.readiness_rationale: The comparison is settled enough to act on, though Automation Coverage is the one factor still worth firming up before committing fully.

fac_automation_rate.specific_action: Pilot the triage automation on a sample of tickets and measure actual coverage achieved before full rollout.
fac_automation_rate.rationale: This factor has the most unresolved influence on which lever looks stronger in this model.
fac_automation_rate.decision_hygiene: Estimate the likely coverage rate before looking at the pilot data.

edge_automation_response.trigger_description: If the link from Automation Coverage to Response Time weakens, coverage gains would translate into less improvement.
edge_automation_response.consequence: In that case, more runs would support Hire Two Support Engineers rather than Automate Tier One Triage.

flip_thresholds.narrative: If Automation Coverage moves from 58% to 31%, more runs would support a different option.

key_assumptions: The link from Automation Coverage to Response Time assumes the automation performs close to its modelled effect once live.
The brief frames the goal as picking a lever rather than a target response time, so no numeric threshold is being scored here.

decision_quality_prompts.question: This failed because Automation Coverage never reached the modelled level, what would you have wanted to see sooner?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: The comparison is settled enough to act on, but it rests on a factor that is not yet firmly evidenced.

decision_quality_prompts.question: What would make you switch to Hire Two Support Engineers instead of Automate Tier One Triage?
decision_quality_prompts.applies_because: Automate Tier One Triage holds a clear majority of runs in this model, so it is worth naming what would overturn that.

pre_mortem.failure_scenario: Automate Tier One Triage failed to cut Response Time because Automation Coverage came in well below the modelled level.
warning_signs: Pilot automation coverage tracking noticeably below the assumed level
Ticket volume rising faster than the automation can absorb
pre_mortem.mitigation: Run a small pilot to confirm achievable automation coverage before committing to full rollout.
